title: Reusable coset-state reflections for quantum shift search

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the fixed-copy quantum shift-search algorithm in proof.md uses n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, and exactly k = n+24 independent ideal DCP source copies on every execution branch. For n >= 2 it performs r = floor(floor(sqrt(9L))/4) iterations of the controlled witness-projector reflection and candidate diffusion defined in proof.md. For n = 1 it tests candidate 0 on all k copies and outputs 0 if all tests pass, or 1 otherwise. This algorithm recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 2/3. In the challenge model its worst-case total work is T(N,s) = O(2^{n/2} n^5), with uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^{n/2} n^5 and exact growth index 1. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with the two workspace bounds, sample bound, and clean-input error model below.

For the same fixed-copy quantum shift-search algorithm and configuration in proof.md, with n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, k = n+24 source copies, r = floor(floor(sqrt(9L))/4) iterations when n >= 2, and the stated n = 1 branch, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak allocated classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n^2) bits. Its uniform bit-length envelope B_C(n) = n^2 has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with the stated total-work, quantum-workspace, and sample bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3 under the clean-input error model below.

For the same fixed-copy quantum shift-search algorithm and configuration in proof.md, with n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, k = n+24 source copies, r = floor(floor(sqrt(9L))/4) iterations when n >= 2, and the stated n = 1 branch, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak allocated quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n^2) qubits. Its uniform bit-length envelope B_Q(n) = n^2 has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This includes all retained source copies and ancillas and holds jointly with the stated total-work, classical-workspace, and sample bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3 under the clean-input error model below.

For the same fixed-copy quantum shift-search algorithm and configuration in proof.md, with n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, k = n+24 source copies, r = floor(floor(sqrt(9L))/4) iterations when n >= 2, and the stated n = 1 branch, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired is exactly n+24 on every execution branch, hence O(n). The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = n has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This count includes every acquired copy, with no additional copies for failed outcomes, and holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3 under the clean-input error model below.

For the same fixed-copy quantum shift-search algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, k = n+24 source copies, r = floor(floor(sqrt(9L))/4) iterations when n >= 2, and the stated n = 1 branch, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0. All Q = n+24 acquired source copies must be independent ideal coset states, so no malformed copies are permitted under this guarantee. Under this promise, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 2/3 jointly with all four stated resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
